stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan set to cross north Andhra-south Odisha coast around noon today
stories.summary: The severe cyclonic storm was over the west-central Bay of Bengal on Thursday night and is expected to cross between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha around noon, with winds of 90-100 km/h gusting to 110 km/h. Odisha says over one lakh people have been moved to safety, more than 9,000 shelters are open and over 300 rescue teams, including NDRF, are deployed. Some trains have been cancelled or rescheduled.
stories.why_it_matters: It is the third cyclone to hit the Andhra coast in under a month, threatening crops, ports and rail links along the east coast.
stories.note: Single source: All India Radio. Landfall forecast as of Thursday night; check IMD for updates.

stories.headline: Modi tells FICCI October goods exports hit a record of nearly $50 billion
stories.summary: At FICCI's centenary convention in New Delhi, the Prime Minister said goods exports last month were close to $50 billion, the highest for any month, and that India is expected to grow about 7%. He asked companies to plan long-term investment around India's interests, compete globally rather than rely on the home market, and use recent trade deals.
stories.why_it_matters: Record exports help the trade balance and the rupee at a time of high oil prices.
stories.note: Single source: All India Radio (PM's speech).

impact.why: Strong exports bring in more dollars, a small support for the rupee.

stories.headline: Amit Shah says police stations will follow one national anti-terror strategy
stories.summary: Opening the NIA's two-day anti-terror conference in New Delhi, the Home Minister said the Centre is building a system that links police stations to state police chiefs under a common counter-terror plan. He asked every state's Anti-Terrorism Squad to strengthen its cyber units and said cutting off terror funding is essential.

stories.headline: Kushner says Russia is 'comfortable' with NATO-style guarantees for Ukraine
stories.summary: New since last night: after the Berlin meeting of Ukraine's allies, US envoy Jared Kushner said Russia is comfortable with postwar security guarantees modelled on NATO's Article 5, as part of a wider package that serves US interests. Germany's Merz called the Shenzhen summit a 'photo op' and said Europe must be at the table; Putin said he is not against European participation and proposed talks in Moscow. No date was set for talks with Russia.
stories.why_it_matters: A Russian acceptance of strong guarantees would remove one of the biggest blocks to a ceasefire deal.
stories.note: Claim by US envoy Kushner; Russia has not publicly confirmed it. Single source: Al Jazeera.

image.alt: Zelensky, Merz, Macron and Kushner at a Coalition of the Willing press conference in Berlin

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia says a Houthi attack damaged a tower in Riyadh's financial district
stories.summary: Saudi authorities say Houthi missile fire hit a tower in Riyadh's financial centre on Thursday; no casualties were reported. Qatar, Kuwait and the Gulf Cooperation Council condemned the attack. In Yemen, the Houthi health ministry says strikes on Sanaa killed 10 people over two days as the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis trade fire.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on the Saudi capital widen the Gulf war and add risk to oil supply.
stories.note: Claims by Saudi authorities and the Houthi health ministry; not independently confirmed. Single source: Al Jazeera.

impact.why: Attacks on Saudi Arabia raise the risk to Gulf oil supply.

stories.headline: US approved sales of over 879,000 AI chips to Chinese firms, House documents show
stories.summary: Documents released by the House Foreign Affairs Committee show the Commerce Department approved the sales, to buyers including Alibaba and Tencent, as of May; some went to firms the Pentagon lists as Chinese military companies. Nvidia and AMD made 3.4 million requests from December to May. Rep. Brian Mast says two companies named in Nvidia's applications are suspected smuggling fronts.
stories.note: Single source: CNBC. Smuggling-front claim is by Rep. Mast.

impact.why: More scrutiny of its China sales adds pressure on the chipmaker.

stories.headline: Former Bangladesh leader Muhammad Yunus's family home set on fire, police say
stories.summary: Police say attackers set fire to part of Yunus's ancestral home in Chittagong late on Wednesday; the blaze was put out quickly and no one was hurt. It came amid protests by the banned Awami League marking a year since Sheikh Hasina, who lives in India, was sentenced to death in absentia. Two BNP members were killed in clashes in Gopalganj.

stories.headline: AI sell-off: Wall Street drops over 2%, Dow below 50,000; Asian tech stocks tumble
stories.summary: US stocks reversed early gains on Thursday: the S&P 500 fell 2.0% to 7,175.83, the Nasdaq 2.3% to 23,879.20 and the Dow 2.2% to 49,097.06, its first close under 50,000 since June. Anthropic's debut failed to revive AI shares and Nvidia hit a 52-week low. On Friday morning SoftBank fell about 16%, Tokyo Electron 7%, SK Hynix 6% and Korea's Kospi 3.7%.
stories.why_it_matters: A global tech sell-off can hit Indian IT stocks and foreign inflows when Dalal Street opens today.

impact.why: Investors are dumping AI-linked shares after a weak reaction to Anthropic's debut.
Global tech weakness usually weighs on Indian IT shares.
Risk-off mood pulled Bitcoin down over 2%.

stories.headline: Anthropic ends first day up 17% at $97.17 after opening at $111.50
stories.summary: Update: Anthropic's shares opened 34% above the $83 IPO price, briefly valuing it at about $2 trillion, then gave up half the gain to close at $97.17. CNBC puts its fully diluted value at about $1.8 trillion. The early lift to the Nasdaq faded and the index closed 2.3% lower.

impact.why: Shares closed well above the IPO price but far below the opening level.

stories.headline: Gold slides another 3% to about $3,563 as yields and Fed hike bets bite
stories.summary: New since last night: US gold futures fell about 3.3% to near $3,563 an ounce early Friday in Asia, after Thursday's drop below $3,700. CNBC cites higher Treasury yields, a firm dollar and talk of further Fed hikes, with one analyst seeing $3,500-3,600. Gold is now more than a third below January's record of $5,589.
stories.why_it_matters: Cheaper gold lowers India's import bill but hits gold loan firms and jewellers' inventories.

impact.why: Higher US yields and a strong dollar keep pushing gold lower.
Silver tends to follow gold in a broad metals sell-off.

forex_results.why: Factory activity slowed far more than the 20.6 forecast, weighing on the dollar.
